requirements_summary: Workloads: real-time chat support for enterprise shippers (~60% traffic), document search/SLAs for manifests (25%), reranking for internal freight search (15%)
Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for chat generate flows (99 target critical for SLAs)
Throughput targets: steady-state ~120 QPS of generation calls during daytime, peak bursts up to 600 QPS for EOD batch windows (30-min windows twice per day)
Token profile: avg 220 tokens/request (including prompt + expected generation), avg tokens/sec per request ~80 tokens/sec during streaming
Availability: 99.95% target; maintenance windows acceptable with 6-hour advance notice and failover policy
Routing/fallback: must support policy-based routing -> dedicated pool, fallback to hosted verified model (lower cost) on overload
Data controls: retention controls (7-day ephemeral caching preferred), ability to pin models and image-level audit logs
sizing_workshop_outcomes: Baseline calculation: steady-state 120 QPS * 220 tokens = 26,400 tokens/sec aggregate; with batching efficiency expected token/sec cost reduction ~1.6x
Peak calculation: 600 QPS * 220 tokens = 132,000 tokens/sec during 30-min spikes; planning safety margin x1.4 -> ~185k tokens/sec provisioned
GPU mapping: H100 80GB equivalents estimated — 6 GPUs baseline to meet steady-state p95 goal with batching and KV caching; 18 GPUs reserved to meet peak throughput with <p95 targets
Autoscale/burst model: dedicated pool sized to 18 GPUs reserved + 6 GPU burst buffer (or cross-region fallback) for extreme spikes
Latency tradeoffs: quantization (4-bit) on reranking models acceptable; chat generation uses fp16 on optimized kernels to preserve quality and tail latency
SLA ask: target 99.95% uptime, latency SLO credits for p99 breaches, guaranteed reserved throughput during contracted windows (EOD spikes)
recommended_capacity_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot: 30 days): Reserve 6 H100-equivalent GPUs in VPC private deployment; enable prefix KV caching for common prompts; run canary traffic (10% production) — goal: validate steady-state costs and latency SLOs

Phase 2 (Reserve for SLAs): Contract 18 GPU reserved pool (monthly commit) with configured scheduled maintenance windows and automated fallback to hosted models for overflow; include 6 GPU burst capacity for short windows

Phase 3 (Optimization): Deploy Redwood Optimize recommendations — tune batching thresholds, adjust quantization for reranking models, set model routing rules (low-latency vs cost-optimized), and enable token-level cost dashboards
Contracting notes: require KMS integration clause, data residency addendum for EU customers, and explicit SLA language on reserved throughput during two daily EOD windows
